subject: babaYagaHut
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a reasonably detailed module for a hut on giant chicken legs, aiming for around 150 parts, keeping it mostly static scenery without rigged joints for simplicity.

I'm sketching proportions: a 3m-wide hut atop 2m legs for roughly 5m total height, with two clawed feet planted at ground level supporting a floor platform. The hut itself is a log cabin built from stacked, alternating horizontal cylinders with notched corners and lighter log-end discs, plus an arched front door with folk-style ornamentation.

Beyond that I'm adding a porch step, carved red-and-blue platbands around the door, small shuttered windows glowing warm, and a steep plank gable roof topped with a carved horse-head ridge log and scalloped bargeboards. A few touches round it out — a smoky chimney, a small glowing skull lantern near the porch, and sunburst/rosette folk-art carvings on the gable.

I'm now working out log-wall construction using a rod helper for the stacked log layers, sizing the radius and spacing of each layer to build the wall height up from the floor level.

So the full structure stacks to around 6.3 units tall with roof and ridge pole included, which feels proportionate for a diorama-scale hut. I'm defining the wall footprint dimensions and figuring out how front/back logs and side logs need to offset vertically at the corners so they interleave correctly instead of intersecting.

For the door, I'm cutting the front wall logs into two segments on either side of a 0.9-wide, 1.5-tall gap, and for the windows I'm just attaching frame assemblies that protrude slightly from the side log walls rather than cutting the logs themselves.

Now I'm working out the floor platform as a flat box with support beams underneath, and planning the chicken legs with hip joints and feathered thigh sections built from scaled spheres.

For the lower leg, I'm shaping the tarsus as a curved sweep bending forward toward the ankle, then adding spread toes -- three pointing forward at different angles and one pointing back for the chicken foot.

Still working out ring orientation...

Now moving to the roof: each slope spans from the ridge down to the eave edge, so I'm sizing boxes to match that span's length and width, then rotating them about the z-axis so they tilt at the correct slope angle on each side.

For shingle texture, I'm planning rows of small log-like rods laid along the slope direction, spaced across the width, colored in alternating greys and mossy tones to give a weathered look.

For the gables, I'm sketching triangular wood panels at the front and back with a decorative solar sun disc motif made of a central circle and radiating triangular rays, done in a Slavic folk style.

Then I'm planning the bargeboard trim along the roof edges with hanging pendant details, plus a ridge log running the length of the roof with a carved horse-head finial at the front end.

Still shaping the horse-head outline coordinates...

Checking that edges E-F and H-I don't cross confirms the outline is clean, so I'll skip smoothing and add simple details like a dark eye disc, red mane scallops, and a yellow bridle, mirroring the shape for the back half. Now I'm placing a chimney box on the structure.

Adding chimney and smoke spheres...

I'm also designing an arched door with painted ornaments -- gold bands, a lock, cross-planks, and a flower rosette -- set into the front opening with a doorframe.

For the frame, I'm sweeping curved rods from the base up and over the arch, then adding a broader outer frame in yellow, and cutting the log layers to fit the arch gap up to around height 1.55. Then I'm adding a few porch steps at the front leading down from the raised platform floor.

Rather than long stairs, I'm switching to a leaning wooden ladder with two angled rails and eight rungs reaching from the floor down to the ground, extending the footprint slightly but keeping the proportions reasonable. Next I'm placing windows on the side walls.

Adding flower-ornament shutters and rosette details...

Now I'm figuring out the gable pelmet band and matching the gable triangle's base and width to the roof eave geometry so the trim lines up with the log wall tops.

Adding a decorative band of rotated diamond shapes along the gable, then designing a skull-topped lantern stake for the porch with glowing orange eyes, placed on both sides as a signature Halloween element. I'm also considering small feather tufts wrapped around the thigh using a ring of cones.

Still working out leg positions...

Toe placement puts the spread within a safe range for the ladder. I'm shaping each toe as a slight curved sweep with a tapered radius and adding a dark claw spike at the tip, checking that it doesn't dip too far below the floor plane, and I still need to add the back-facing toe.

Now I'm settling on the color palette: warm browns for the log structure with lighter cut ends and visible rings, plus folk-art reds, blues, golds, and cream against darker tones, orange-yellow for the legs, dark claws, mossy green, and alternating roof shingle browns. I'm also considering whether to add a small ground base or mound with grass beneath the feet to round out the diorama feel.

I'm working out the ground disc geometry -- figuring the height offset so the hut's legs sink properly into a raised earthen base, then planning to add a grassy top with little details like mushroom tufts and a couple of simple stacked-cone fir trees in the background for folk-art charm.

Now I'm setting up the builder scaffolding, importing the geometry helpers and a glow kit, and defining leg/ladder coordinates relative to the ground height before writing the actual construction calls for the hut's structure.

Writing log wall layout logic...

Adding end discs only to outer log ends, skipping the inner cut ends near the door, which keeps part count manageable; I'll leave moss off the walls for now and reserve it for the roof instead.

Checking the interleaved corner logs with their offset and radius, the overlap should be solid enough that gaps aren't visible once the roof and floor cover things. I need to cap the side logs at layer 6 so they don't poke above the front wall's layer 7, then add a wall plate beam along the top to tie everything together.

Now I'm working out the gable geometry with floor level at 2.6, giving a wall top around 4.68. I'm placing the roof eaves and ridge points, computing the slope angle, and adjusting the gable triangle's vertices so its edges sit just under the roof slab's lower surface at each point.

Next I'm laying out the shingle rows along the roof slope using a direction vector and normal offset, spacing them every 0.26 units with small rods colored alternately, plus scattered moss as flattened spheres. I'm also sizing the ridge log and planning end caps at each gable peak where the ridge meets the structure.

Now I'm figuring out scale for the decorative horse-head finial (konyok), settling on roughly 0.8-1.0x so it reads as suitably large and majestic against the hut roof, and planning the decorative mane scallops, eye, bridle band, and neck rosette positioned along the back edge using local z-offsets at each end.

I'm also planning gable decoration -- a sun disc with ring rays, flanking rosettes near the peak, pelmet diamonds, and glowing side windows -- while deciding to skip a hanging pendant under the gable peak. For the door, I'm working out the front log surface position and door slab thickness relative to the door center.

Now I'm positioning the door slab flush against the log face, extruding it along the x-axis with the correct thickness direction, then adding decorative details: vertical gold rods, horizontal iron straps with studs, a top rosette, a ring handle, and a carved platband frame following a curved path with two nested radii.

I'm defining the arched door outline and threshold points, then figuring out where the log courses need to be cut away to leave the doorway gap, matching the arch's peak height to the log layer boundaries so the platband frame sits correctly against the opening.

Now I'm adding the decorative pediment above the door — a scalloped kokoshnik-style crown shape extruded in layered gold, red, and blue with a small yellow accent dot — before moving on to a reusable skull-placement helper for the assembly.

For the skulls, I'm defining a cranium sphere scaled slightly for shape, with a cheek/jaw box, glowing-orange eye sockets, nose, and a teeth row, mounted atop rod stakes placed at the front corners of the platform so they face outward. Then I'm sizing the overall platform box and floor to fit, centering it around z=0.1 with roughly a 3.7 unit footprint.

Now I'm working out the porch area in front of the hut walls, placing stakes and a railing with a gap left open for the ladder, plus positioning the ladder's sloped side rails and rungs leading up to the platform. I'm also adding support beams underneath the floor as horizontal logs spaced along the x-axis.

Writing hip joint and window frame code...

Checking the frame and glass positioning math to make sure the glass sits properly against the window frame without clipping through it, then placing the side windows and a back window centered on the rear wall.

Now I'm adding a triangular pediment above the side window in red with a gold dot accent, skipping extra ornamental elements like friezes and corner posts to avoid over-engineering, and sketching a brick-colored chimney box positioned near the roof.

Then I'm figuring out the chimney cap dimensions and placing a rising sequence of light gray smoke puffs above it with drifting offsets, before moving to build the ground using a lathe-based outline for the earth base.

I'll flatten the grass top at G=0.18 to keep it simple, then add scene details: stepping stones leading to the ladder, a few mushrooms, and two fir trees made of trunk cylinders with dark green cones for the foliage.

For color palette I'm settling on warm feather tones for the thighs, yellow for legs and toes, dark brown claws, and a muted gold for the scale ring. Now I'm writing the foot helper function defining toe positions and angles...

Writing toe geometry...

Realizing sweep points orient along the normal rather than tangent, I switch to a path-based approach so cylinders follow the tangent direction instead, computing radius manually as a linear taper and adding a backward-pointing spike partway along the tarsus. Then I move on to building feather rings around the thigh using a frame positioned near its base.

Writing rosette helper...

Still arranging ring geometry...

Now I'm designing the gable trim: alternating red and gold diamond shapes along the gable base, with a blue support board beneath, and considering a deep blue background for the gable plate to match a Slavic folk-art palette of blue, red, and gold.

I'm adding a gold sun motif at the gable peak with red triangular rays and a smaller inner red dot, then planning bargeboards that follow the roof slope edges on both the front and back gables to frame the sun decoration.

For the pendant decorations hanging below the bargeboards, I'm placing a row of small golden spheres along each edge, spaced evenly across the roof slope and dropping slightly below the board line to create a scalloped hanging effect.

Now I'm thinking about adding small windows flanking the front door since the front wall is narrow -- framed boxes with glass and a soft glow, positioned symmetrically on either side at a comfortable height, skipping shutters to keep it simple but still giving a welcoming lit look.

Switching to the roof, I'm computing the slab geometry as a rotated box so each side slopes down from the ridge to the eave, verifying the rotation angle and center position line up correctly for both sides. Then I'm figuring out how to place individual shingles along that sloped surface, offsetting them slightly above the slab so they sit visibly on top rather than clipping into it.

I'm also working out the ridge cap as a small horizontal rod with capped ends, and designing the decorative horse-head ornament (konyok) at each gable end -- positioning the extruded head shape, scaling it down, and placing small red spheres along the mane edge for detail.

Now I'm settling on a warm cream-gold color for the carved wood look with a reddish mane accent, and planning to write the final code with a helper function for coordinate points and a part-adding function that handles position and optional direction for each piece.

I'm sketching a skull helper that builds the cranium as a scaled sphere, the jaw as a box beneath it, dark eye sockets with small glowing orange highlights, a dark nose box, and a few thin boxes for teeth, all positioned relative to the skull's center.

Now I'm placing stakes with rods and skulls mounted along the fence line, adding mushrooms built from hemisphere geometry caps with small white dot spheres stuck on top and cylindrical stalks, and planning to add trees next.

I'm estimating around 450 lines total and moving on to door details—positioning the door extrusion at the correct offset, then adding vertical gold trim rods and horizontal iron straps as thin boxes across the door face.

Switching the straps to red with gold studs, adding a circular rosette near the top, and placing a torus-shaped door handle that's naturally oriented in the right plane without extra rotation. I'm also adding a small threshold step box at the door's base, checking that its height lines up with the platform floor top.

Finishing up with the floor plank box, double-checking the lathe outline syntax and typing for the tree shape, then placing the fir cone geometry at the right height before writing the final code.
